name: zlib
notes: linux: shared-pass -- tools/crt-cc/tools/crt-c++'s -shared mode originally statically linked non-PIC libc.a on every OS, a hard ld error on Linux's stricter ELF relocations (R_AARCH64_ADR_PREL_PG_HI21 against stdin/stdout/stderr); fixed by linking the already-built shared libc.so/libm.so/libdl.so/libc++.so counterparts instead for shared_mode on Linux. That alone wasn't enough for runtime resolution: none of this project's own shared libraries set an explicit -soname, so libz.so.1.3.1's DT_NEEDED recorded the bare 'libc.so', which ld.so then re-resolved at runtime against the host's own /lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/libc.so (a linker-script stub, not a real ELF image) instead of this project's sysroot -- fixed by adding -Wl,-rpath,${CRT_SYSROOT}/lib to shared_mode's Linux link flags. ldd on a real Linux aarch64 machine confirmed the fix: libz.so.1.3.1's libc.so/libm.so/libdl.so/libc++.so dependencies all resolve to this project's own sysroot, not the host's.

macos: shared-pass -- otool -l .../libz.dylib | grep -A2 LC_RPATH confirmed both expected LC_RPATH entries are present (.../sysroot/lib and .../port-tests/install/lib, added the same way as the Linux fix), so the stray @rpath/libc.dylib dependency introduced by zlib's own LDSHAREDLIBC=-lc flag (unconditional except on MinGW; ld64 prefers the sibling libc.dylib over the same-named static libc.a when both exist on the search path) now resolves correctly at load time.

Builds both static libz.a and shared libz.so.1.3.1 (plus the libz.so/libz.so.1 SONAME symlinks) into PORT_PREFIX; configure_args was changed from ["--static"] to [] so zlib's own default shared=1 behavior applies on every OS, now that Windows can build and load shared objects too (see below).

target_overrides.windows.env undefines _WIN32/_WIN32_WCE/__WIN32__/WIN32/_MSC_VER so zlib stays on its generic POSIX path when the Windows CRT wrapper uses a Windows LLVM target; scoped to Windows only since these macros are never predefined on macOS/Linux anyway.

target_overrides.windows.env also sets RANLIB=true because the optional zlib ranlib step is redundant for the LLVM archive path and used to expose a Windows mksh subshell status quirk; macOS/Linux use the real host ranlib (the crt-port-build.py default) since neither has that quirk.
Windows CRT-shell builds currently run make serially and pass SHELL=/system/bin/mksh so recipe commands use the project shell/process path.

windows: shared-pass -- tools/crt-cc/tools/crt-c++ gained -shared/-dynamiclib support (dllcrt.o + /entry:crtDllMainCRTStartup + /DLL) and libc/src/arch/windows/common/syscall.c's __crt_sys_symlink() went from an -ENOSYS stub to a real CreateSymbolicLinkA()-backed implementation, unblocking zlib's Makefile SONAME step (`ln -s libz.so.1.3.1 libz.so`) which previously failed the whole shared build. Verified past 'it built' into 'it actually works': zlib's own examplesh/minigzipsh test binaries, built and dynamically linked against the freshly built libz.so.1.3.1, ran a real compress/uncompress/gzip round trip successfully.

windows: CreateSymbolicLinkA() with SYMBOLIC_LINK_FLAG_ALLOW_UNPRIVILEGED_CREATE still requires Windows Developer Mode to be enabled (Settings > Privacy & security > For developers) for a non-elevated process -- without it, CreateSymbolicLinkA fails with ERROR_PRIVILEGE_NOT_HELD (now mapped to EPERM in map_windows_error() rather than falling through to a generic EIO). This is a one-time machine setting, not something this project's build can turn on for itself (it's a real Windows system setting, not a build flag).

windows: __crt_sys_readlink() went from an -ENOSYS stub to a real DeviceIoControl(FSCTL_GET_REPARSE_POINT)-backed implementation after a *rebuild* of this exact recipe (an install/lib directory that already has libz.so/libz.so.1 symlinks in it from a previous run) failed with 'rm: .../libz.so: Function not implemented' -- traced to toybox's dirtree.c (shared by every directory-walking applet, including rm) calling readlinkat() on every symlink entry it visits to populate try->symlink, which propagated the stub's -ENOSYS straight into rm aborting. Fixed generally in libc/src/arch/windows/common/syscall.c, not specific to this recipe; verified by re-running this same rebuild twice in a row (exercising the rm-of-an-existing-symlink path) with no error either time.
